purpose: Retains the GitHub API readback of the dismissal that docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md records for Dependabot alert 16: GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (critical; next 16.2.0 through 16.3.5, fixed in 16.3.6) on the frozen macOS variant's evidence/artifacts/macos-application-20260924/variant/package.json, dismissed as not_used on 2026-10-03. Dependabot alerts come from GitHub's dependency graph, whose inputs are the repository's manifests and lock files and dependency submissions; an OSV-Scanner config is not among them (cause). The alert is therefore independent of the scope of the OSV exception in .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml: the 2026-09-30 OSV review of the same advisory for the same frozen artifact could not suppress it, and the alert needed a decision of its own. The record keeps the dismissal command, a read-only readback of the alert, the cause, the authority and its limits, the reasoning the dismissal relies on, its review date and overturn, and the tests that guard it: a tripwire for direct references to the artifact and a test that ties the recheck to the frozen OSV exception's date.
authorization: The authority is the user's message of 2026-10-03 to the coordinating session, given after that session listed Dependabot alert 16 among its open items. It asked that session to resolve its own open items and to hand anything gated on the other WSL to a lane prompt in a terminal profile; this record describes the message and neither quotes nor retains it. Its limits: the message asks for the session's open items to be resolved and does not name this alert, a dismissal or not_used; the session took it to cover alert 16, which it had listed among those items. The precedent is analogous, not identical, and was later superseded by a rename (reasoning.precedent): the closure record dismissed as not_used the alerts on a file that nothing installs (section 8, 'Fixture alerts dismissed': alerts 7-15 on the grype positive-control fixture), but that fixture's not_used handling was requested by the gap-resolution session that owns the fixture (section 8, 'Fixture kept out of future security PRs'), whereas the tree records no owner for the frozen macOS lock (section 3) and no owner asked for this dismissal. The dismissal adds no exception: it relies on the 2026-09-30 reachability review of the same advisory for the same frozen lock. It lasts until the alert is reopened, since nothing expires it; the recheck is tied to the frozen OSV exception, whose removal or changed ignoreUntil fails tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py, and to that module's tripwire (review_date, overturn). The Codex review of PR #635 (at 6cd585e9) found that no receipt held the API response, and later reviews of the PR asked for the cause, authorization, review date and guard scope stated here. The readback is a read-only GET.
evidence_class: One read-only GitHub REST API GET of the alert, made with the gh CLI on this host, whose --jq selection keeps only the fields under readback.result (no account field, no token, no URL). The PATCH is recorded from the dismissal at 2026-10-03T04:51:57Z and was not re-run; the response of that call was not retained, so the readback's state, dismissed_reason, dismissed_at and dismissed_comment are the retained evidence of its effect. The cause cites two GitHub Docs pages read on 2026-10-03. The reasoning cites files read at checked_commit, the base PR #635 was rebased onto before round 7 (#619 changed none of them since 652c15ac, and #639 and #620 none since dcae68bd, where they were first read); #634 (9b0b8d6d), which round 7 rebased the PR onto, changed none of them either, nor did #636 (4ced2923), on which round 8 rebuilt it (it changed AGENTS.md and manifests/evidence.json). The ruleset fields in limitations are those of .github/main-ruleset.json at checked_commit, and one read-only GET of the rules that apply to main (gh api repos/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/rules/branches/main, filtered with --jq to the pull_request rule, at 2026-10-03T08:37:44Z) returned the same two values for ruleset 23739774. Relayed by the coordinating session that received the user's message, and not observed by the workers that wrote this record: the authorization's description of that message, the context that the session had listed Dependabot alert 16 among its open items before the message came, and the session's reading of the message as covering alert 16. The conversation is neither retained nor quoted. The review history the authorization and indirect_routes cite (the Codex reviews at 6cd585e9, 7ce51c0a, 06c90dfc and 9faa5c4e, what later reviews asked for, and the convergence round's votes) is as the coordinating session relayed it; this record retains no readback of those reviews. The guard's description and its mutation checks are of the test module committed with this record (guard_mutation_checks.module_sha256); the checks are local fault injection with synthetic scenario fixtures, run in scratch clones on this host and not in CI, and their driver, returned results and the earlier modules the control runs used are retained (guard_mutation_checks.retained); the control runs are on main's d2777ee7 with those modules, which anyone can rebuild. Nothing in the variant was installed, built, served or scanned for this record.
limitations: The readback is the live API state at 2026-10-03T06:58:43Z. The alert's state can change after it (a reopen, or a new alert on the same manifest), so a later read can differ.

This is not a scan of the package or of the lock: the vulnerable range and the first patched version are GitHub's advisory data as the API returned them. The OSV scan of the frozen lock and its dated exception are recorded in evidence/receipts/osv-urllib3-next-20260930.json.

The account that dismissed the alert is not recorded (dismissed_by is left out of the selection on purpose). The PATCH command is kept in the form recorded for the dismissal, with the comment the readback returns.

Like the OSV exception, the dismissal is a statement about this repository only: the repository keeps the variant's package.json and lock, so it says nothing about the application that ran on the Mac on 2026-09-24.

tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py is a tripwire for direct references, not a proof that nothing uses the lock. It misses a route that never spells the artifact directory's name in a file it scans: a step that iterates the paths of the OSV inventory or of FROZEN_LOCKS, a glob such as evidence/artifacts/*/variant, a name assembled from fragments or held outside the repository, a Markdown recipe whose commands someone runs, a file in an excluded class (*.md outside the .claude, .codex, .agents and .devcontainer directories, whose names are compared in any ASCII letter case; evidence/**; manifests/evidence.json; catalogs/**) that its recogniser does not name, such as a JSON launch configuration kept under evidence/**, and text that does not hold the name as ASCII-compatible bytes. Its mutation checks confirmed that the glob, inventory-loop, fragment, Markdown and evidence/** launch-configuration cases pass it (guard_mutation_checks, L1-L5). This record's own retained driver, evidence/artifacts/frozen-variant-guard-mutations-20261003/mutants.py, is such a file: it assembles the artifact directory's name from fragments, so keeping it in the repository adds no line naming the artifact to the scan, which reads .py files under evidence/**; it writes scenario files into the clone its first argument names, runs this module's tests there and installs, builds or serves nothing. The earlier modules kept for the control runs (controls/round3-module.py.txt, round4-module.py.txt and round5-module.py.txt in the same directory) name the artifact directory, but the guard does not read them: they are .txt files under evidence/** with Git mode 100644, no leading #! and no client configuration directory in their path, so its recogniser does not name them; nothing runs them. Names and suffixes are compared as written, so a configuration file inside an excluded class whose name or suffix differs only in letter case from a recognised one (for example PACKAGE.JSON or x.YML under evidence/**) is not read either. That is why the dismissal is also tied to the OSV exception's review (review_date).

The guard is only as strong as review of tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py itself: any part of the module (PINNED_LINES, the tripwire's allowlist; REVIEW_DATE; ARTIFACT_FILES; the recognisers; the excluded classes; or the module as a whole) can be changed or removed in the same change that adds a use, and the main ruleset sets required_approving_review_count 0 and require_code_owner_review false (.github/main-ruleset.json at checked_commit, and the live rules for main read at 2026-10-03T08:37:44Z), so no code owner has to review that edit.

The frozen config's reason says that the live recipe lock pins next 16.3.6. That was true when the reason was written (#546, 2026-09-30); the lock pins 16.3.8 at checked_commit. This record does not edit the config.

dismissal.command: gh api -X PATCH repos/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/dependabot/alerts/16 -f state=dismissed -f dismissed_reason=not_used -f dismissed_comment='Frozen evidence artifact (package.json and lock only, no app source); nothing installs, builds or serves it. Same advisory reviewed for this lock: .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml, evidence/receipts/osv-urllib3-next-20260930.json. Live recipe lock pins next 16.3.6+.'

readback.command: gh api repos/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/dependabot/alerts/16 --jq '{number, state, dismissed_reason, dismissed_at, dismissed_comment, ghsa_id: .security_advisory.ghsa_id, severity: .security_advisory.severity, package: .dependency.package.name, ecosystem: .dependency.package.ecosystem, manifest_path: .dependency.manifest_path, vulnerable_version_range: .security_vulnerability.vulnerable_version_range, first_patched_version: .security_vulnerability.first_patched_version.identifier}'

result.dismissed_comment: Frozen evidence artifact (package.json and lock only, no app source); nothing installs, builds or serves it. Same advisory reviewed for this lock: .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml, evidence/receipts/osv-urllib3-next-20260930.json. Live recipe lock pins next 16.3.6+.

readback.agrees_with_the_record: state dismissed, reason not_used and dismissed_at 2026-10-03T04:51:57Z, as the closure record states

cause.statement: Dependabot raises alerts from GitHub's dependency graph: it 'scans your repository's default branch and sends alerts when' a new vulnerability is added to the GitHub Advisory Database or 'your dependency graph changes', and the graph is 'a summary of the manifest and lock files stored in a repository and any dependencies that are submitted for the repository using the dependency submission API'. An OSV-Scanner config is not among those inputs; it applies only to the scanner invocation it is passed to (security-scan.yml's --config). So the exception in .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml neither reaches nor scopes the alert, which the graph raised from the variant's package.json.

reasoning.frozen_artifact: evidence/artifacts/macos-application-20260924/variant/ holds package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml only (two files, no application source). The lock pins next 16.3.5 at sha256 f1c707b8295e85bd396e49b990de92dc82bc0d58eca1e4e4bef31262d9898cd2, which FROZEN_LOCKS in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py binds; its bytes are hash-bound evidence, so it cannot be bumped.
reasoning.frozen_config: .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml holds one [[IgnoredVulns]] entry, for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j until 2026-12-24, and applies only to that lock's scan. Its reason states that no workflow, script or recipe installs, builds or serves the variant, so no route reaches ImageResponse from anything this repository runs.
reasoning.review: evidence/receipts/osv-urllib3-next-20260930.json: the 2026-09-30 review of the same advisory for the same frozen lock, with the split scan that keeps the exception from reaching any other lock.
reasoning.live_recipe_lock: blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/pnpm-lock.yaml pins next 16.3.8 at checked_commit (since #587, 798ac445, 2026-10-01), outside the advisory's range, and is scanned under the ordinary config, which holds no exception for the advisory. The frozen config's reason, written in #546 (8fc86119, 2026-09-30) when that lock pinned 16.3.6, still says 16.3.6; the clause is older than the lock. The dismissal comment's 'Live recipe lock pins next 16.3.6+' holds for 16.3.8.
reasoning.precedent: Analogous, not identical: Dependabot alerts 7-15 on the grype positive-control fixture were dismissed as not_used because nothing installs the file (closure record, section 8, 'Fixture alerts dismissed'), and that fixture's not_used handling was requested by the gap-resolution session that owns it ('Fixture kept out of future security PRs'). The frozen macOS lock has no recorded owner (section 3), and no owner requested this dismissal (authorization). On 2026-09-25 the repository superseded those dismissals by renaming the fixture to requirements.txt.fixture (commit 636751ae, PR #224; section 8, 'Superseded (2026-09-25)'), after which alerts 7-15 read fixed (API readback, 2026-10-03); indirect_routes records the same course for this lock.

review_date: The dismissal carries no expiry (the PATCH sets state, dismissed_reason and dismissed_comment only) and lasts until the alert is reopened. It is reviewed with the OSV exception for the same advisory and lock: recheck alert 16 when the exception in .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml (ignoreUntil 2026-12-24) is renewed, changed or removed, or when tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py fails. The trigger is mechanical: that module's FrozenOsvExceptionReviewTests reads the TOML with tomllib and fails with 'recheck Dependabot alert 16 (reopen it unless the renewed exception's reasoning still holds) and update this pinned date' when the exception for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j is absent or duplicated, its ignoreUntil is not 2026-12-24 (a TOML date-time on that day counts as the date, as in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py) or it has a key besides id, ignoreUntil and reason; a changed reason fails the tripwire's pinned reason line (guard_mutation_checks N3, N8, X11, X12).
guard: tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py, a tripwire for direct references to the artifact, not a proof that nothing uses the lock. It fails when the artifact directory holds a file besides run-summary.json, variant/package.json and variant/pnpm-lock.yaml, on disk or in Git (OS metadata files aside; tracked paths compared in any ASCII letter case, since a case-insensitive file system checks a differently cased path out into the same directory; a missing file or an absent directory passes, since removing the variant or the artifact is not a use), the whole directory being watched because a script beside variant/ reaches the lock by a relative path that never names the directory; when a scanned file names the artifact directory (the bytes of macos-application-20260924, matched in any ASCII letter case with both sides lower-cased, so a path through the parent directory, a joined path or a differently cased path counts) on a line the module does not pin; when a pinned line is no longer found, so that a broken scope rule cannot drop a pinned file silently; when the variant's package.json or lock no longer pins next 16.3.5, or the lock's sha256 differs from the value FROZEN_LOCKS binds; when .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml holds no exception for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, more than one, or one whose ignoreUntil is not 2026-12-24 or that has a key besides id, ignoreUntil and reason (review_date); and when git ls-files cannot run (it fails rather than skips). Scope, as the code applies it: every file git ls-files lists is scanned except four excluded classes, *.md outside the client configuration directories (documentation), evidence/** and manifests/evidence.json (retained evidence and the hash registry) and catalogs/** (catalog data); blueprints/**/*.json is scanned like any other file. Inside the excluded classes the scan reads only what its recogniser names: the names in CONFIG_NAMES (package.json, lerna.json, nx.json, turbo.json, rush.json, deno.json, deno.jsonc, devcontainer.json and .devcontainer.json); tsconfig*.json and jsconfig*.json; every file under a directory in CONFIG_DIRECTORIES, at any depth, which holds .devcontainer and the client configuration directories .claude, .codex and .agents (an agent, command or skill definition there is Markdown whose YAML frontmatter can declare hooks or tools that the client runs, so Markdown there is read as configuration); the suffixes in CONFIG_SUFFIXES (.toml, .yml, .yaml) and SCRIPT_SUFFIXES (.sh, .bash, .zsh, .ksh, .fish, .ps1, .psm1, .bat, .cmd, .py, .pyw, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .jsx, .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .rb, .pl, .lua, .go, .rs, .mk); the names in BUILD_NAMES (Makefile, makefile, GNUmakefile, Justfile, justfile, Procfile, Rakefile, Taskfile); Dockerfile*, Containerfile* and *.dockerfile; content that starts with #!; Git's executable mode (100755); and symbolic links (120000). Names and suffixes are compared as written and the directory names in CONFIG_DIRECTORIES in any ASCII letter case (a client on a case-insensitive file system loads .CLAUDE as it loads .claude); any other file there is not scanned. For a symbolic link the scan reads the path that the link holds, not the file it points to, and a file that cannot be read (a submodule, or a file missing from the work tree) is skipped. A pin is the sha256 of one referencing line as written, stripped. At checked_commit plus the module it pins 56 referencing lines in 18 files, its own constant line included; round 4 added the 25 lines that scanning blueprints/**/*.json exposed (23 in blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/experiment-macos-20260924.json, and one in each of the two retained OSV-Scanner JSON outputs of the 2026-09-30 relocks), and round 5's client-directory rule, which brings 12 tracked Markdown files into the scan (the 11 agent definitions in .claude/agents and adoption/scaffold/.agents/skills/README.md), exposed none. Its failure messages for a possible new use say to reopen Dependabot alert 16 and remove the frozen OSV exception (config, inventory key and FROZEN_LOCKS row) before installing, building or serving from the lock. Its stated limits are in limitations.
indirect_routes: Decided 2026-10-03 by the coordinating session, after the Codex review at 06c90dfc asked to cover indirect routes such as inventory iteration and workspace globs or leave the alert open: the dismissal stands for now, the guard stays a tripwire for direct references, and the indirect routes stay stated limits (limitations; rows L1-L5); the same day's convergence round, recorded at (5), chose to supersede the dismissal by renaming the frozen files. The alternatives, and why each was declined (counts at main 4ced2923, by the commands recorded at the end of this field): (1) pin every line that names .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json or .github/osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml (43 lines in 20 files: workflows, tests, blueprint evidence, the OSV inventory and the ordinary OSV config), so that every edit there would trip this guard, while a loop over git ls-files '*package.json' would still pass; (2) pin every line in workflows, scripts and package or build configuration that names pnpm, npm, yarn, bun, npx or corepack as a word (297 lines in 61 files), the same coupling at a larger scale; (3) resolve the working directory of each package-manager command and fail on a dynamic one, a heuristic over shell and YAML that a new form of command evades; (4) reopen the alert, which leaves a critical alert open on bytes that are hash-bound evidence and cannot be bumped; the closure record had dismissed alerts 7-15 on a fixture nothing installs as not_used with no guard (section 8) and superseded that on 2026-09-25 by renaming the fixture (commit 636751ae, PR #224); (5) stop keeping the frozen manifest under names that Dependabot, Scorecard's OSV-Scanner and the coverage test parse, which removes the alert's subject; it changes the frozen artifact, the OSV inventory, the frozen OSV config, FROZEN_LOCKS, security-scan.yml and the experiment record, so it was left to a separate decision. That decision was taken the same day: a convergence round (Claude and GPT-6 research, then two GPT-6 Astra and two Claude Opus votes, with the GitHub/CI lane session's input) chose to rename both variant files byte-for-byte to .frozen and to stop scanning them, as the repository did for a captured npm lock (docs/decisions/2026-09-25-longmemeval-frozen-npm-lock.md) and the grype fixture (PR #224), because a scan of bytes that cannot be bumped yields only exceptions, and any new advisory on the lock would fail the required osv-scanner check on every pull request. A follow-up pull request makes that change and records the votes; this dismissal and the guard stand until it merges. No workspace configuration (pnpm-workspace.yaml, lerna.json, rush.json, nx.json, turbo.json or a package.json workspaces field) is tracked at 4ced2923. The indirect routes have a dated backstop. Once the frozen exception's ignoreUntil (2026-12-24) is reached, the required osv-scanner job fails in its unittest preflight (FrozenScanTests, .github/workflows/security-scan.yml:75-78) before OSV-Scanner runs, and the required validate job's full suite fails IgnorePolicyTests; both go through ignore_entry_problems in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py, which rejects an expired entry and one more than 90 days ahead. Renewing or changing the entry fails this module's review-date test, which asks for alert 16 to be rechecked, unless the same change also edits REVIEW_DATE, which no required review covers (limitations). Overturn this decision, besides the conditions in overturn, if a tracked workspace configuration appears, or if a workflow or script that iterates the OSV inventory or the repository's package manifests runs a package manager. Counts: git grep -n -e osv-scanner-lockfiles.json -e osv-scanner-frozen-macos.toml 4ced2923 -- . ':!*.md' ':!evidence/**' ':!catalogs/**' ':!manifests/evidence.json' gives 43 lines (20 files with -l); git grep -n -E '(^|[^[:alnum:]_./-])(pnpm|npm|yarn|bun|npx|corepack)( |$)' 4ced2923 -- '.github/workflows/*' '*.sh' '*.py' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.yml' '*.yaml' 'Makefile' '*/Makefile' 'package.json' '*/package.json' 'Dockerfile*' '*/Dockerfile*' ':!evidence/**' ':!catalogs/**' gives 297 lines (61 files with -l).

guard_mutation_checks.method: Local fault injection with synthetic scenario fixtures, run in scratch clones on one host: not an upstream harness, and not run in CI. The table is the output of the retained runs (retained), round 8's final run and round 9's three control runs: the driver and, for each run, a subdirectory with its results file, per-mutant logs and stdout, in which each clone root is replaced with <clone>, the run's output directory with <out> and the Python installation's prefix with <python>; runs.json gives each run's argument vector, working directory, start and end times, exit code, clone head and module sha256. Round 8 ran the driver from its repository path over all 45 rows in a fresh scratch clone of round 8's content commit (a447a511), the branch rebuilt as one content commit on main 4ced2923 (#636), which carries this module and the driver, and every row came out as expected (final). Round 7 had run the same 45 rows against its first content commit (8f547913), which was never pushed; round 8's run gave the same outcomes, failing tests and messages, and replaces it. Each mutant edited the clone, staged its new files (git ls-files lists only the index; M2, N5 and P1 stay untracked, and P3 is added with git add -f because .gitignore's *.db rule ignores Thumbs.db), ran python3 -m unittest tests.test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and was then restored to a clean git status; X8 ran with no git on PATH. M1a-M4 reconstruct the three mutants of round 2's brief (that round's own table is not retained); M5-M9 are round 3's brief, N1-N3 round 4's, N4-N8 round 5's (N7 for its section 1, N4-N6 for section 2, N8 for section 4) and N9 round 6's; X and P rows are added checks; L rows are the stated limits. Round 4's 33 rows kept their outcomes; M2, M3 and X8 now name the renamed directory tests, which watch the whole artifact directory, and X15's mutant, which makes fold_ascii return its input, also fails the listed-configuration test since round 6 made the client directory comparison use fold_ascii. 'failed' lists the failing tests without their test_ prefix, once each; 'messages' names the failure texts present (reopen: reopen Dependabot alert 16 and remove the frozen OSV exception; stale pin; git: git ls-files could not run; recheck: recheck Dependabot alert 16 (reopen it unless the renewed exception's reasoning still holds) and update this pinned date). The round_N_module fields are runs of the same rows against the earlier modules, which are retained byte for byte (retained.controls). For each, a scratch clone of main's d2777ee7 had that module copied to tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py and committed, and the unmutated tree (M0) passed there: round_5_module (N9) is against the round-5 module (sha256 6006cede80c9df94028fc377dfc4efbbb8c3e283ec99bbf1ad25cd4040ddd054), round_4_module (N4-N8, X13) against the round-4 module (sha256 415d90caf23b81f0d0b4c2a3e3f23316db51f4058cbebed81ef0bf71a0d02242) and round_3_module (N1-N3) against the round-3 module (sha256 3058872c039726e7057addb1e54ea32cd5f24b1f8cbdd449a23befc10ee77bd2). Each of those rows passed there, which shows its gap was real, so these runs exit 1 by design. Round 9 made these runs on that base, which anyone can rebuild from the repository and the retained modules; round 7 had run the same rows in clones of PR #635's earlier commits (4af88b1d, faaa86f9 and a scratch commit on 4af88b1d), with the same outcomes, failing tests and messages. Rounds 4 to 6 ran the same rows with earlier copies of the driver, whose output is not retained: round 4 ran N1-N3 against the round-3 module; round 5 ran its rows in a scratch clone of the PR branch at 4af88b1d with its module committed on it, and N4-N8 and X13 against the round-4 module; and round 6 (the coordinating session, 2026-10-03), after making the module compare the client configuration directory names in any ASCII letter case, added N9 and X16, ran all 45 rows in a scratch clone of the branch with the round-6 module committed and ran N9 against the round-5 module. Round 7's observed outcomes and round_N_module fields equal those this table recorded before it. Round 10 rebased the branch onto main 59f8a1e3 (#653), which changed .github/workflows/validate.yml's timeout and manifests/evidence.json, neither of which names the artifact; the module's tests pass at the rebased head. Round 7 also corrected three rows to the retained output: X15's 'failed' gained the_listed_configuration_kinds_are_scanned_inside_the_record_classes, which the table had missed since round 6 made the client directory comparison use fold_ascii, and N9 and X16 gained the 'failed' and 'messages' fields that round 6 had left out.
